_comment: This file holds ONLY what has to be known before the app can ask the database anything: how to reach the database, and how to bind the listener. Every other setting -- the renderer's address and queue token, the registration code, the memory floor, the catalogue and tag-model paths, the log file and level, the proxy and stack-trace toggles -- is a row in dbo.MachineSetting, keyed by machine name, and is edited at /settings/machine. It is NOT also here: a key lives in one place, so 'I edited the file and nothing changed' cannot happen. Those keys are absent, not commented out.
_bootstrapComment: The four below are still editable from the settings page -- it writes them into appsettings.<Environment>.json, which is gitignored -- but they are read once while the host is built, so a change waits for a restart.

Kestrel._comment: Editor uploads (/forge/upload) are the raw file as-selected -- phone photos and video -- so the ~28.6MB default 413s them. Kept in step with client_max_body_size in deploy/imagegen-nginx.conf.

ConnectionStrings._comment: Defaults to a SQLite file beside the app so an unconfigured install starts and works. For SQL Server, set Database:Provider to SqlServer as well -- the app refuses to start if the two disagree rather than quietly creating an empty database.

TagModel._comment: WriteToSharedCache controls where the tag model downloads and loads its ~900MB artifacts. false (default) uses the pre-cache beside the executable (tagmodel/artifacts in the install folder); true uses the machine-wide shared cache (%LOCALAPPDATA%\ImageGenerationServer\tagmodel\artifacts) that persists across deploys. Read once at startup (before the database is available), so it lives here, not in dbo.MachineSetting -- and honours the TagModel__WriteToSharedCache environment variable to turn it on machine-wide.

Database._comment: Provider is Sqlite or SqlServer, and defaults to Sqlite: it needs no server and no out-of-band schema step. SQL Server is for a deployment sharing one database between several app instances; it expects schema.sql to be applied out-of-band, because the app's login has no DDL rights. Note that dbo.MachineSetting must exist before the app will start -- it is read while the host is being built, and a box whose schema has not been applied fails there rather than booting on code defaults for values somebody believes they set.
Database._schemaComment: EnsureSchemaOnStartup is deliberately NOT set here. It defaults to ON under SQLite (the only way a fresh install can create its own file) and OFF under SQL Server (whose login holds no DDL rights). Setting it here would override that per-provider default for BOTH -- which is what a literal false used to do, leaving a SQLite install unable to create its own schema.
